source.title: Compute-optimal data scaling for neural surrogates via multi-fidelity training
source.authors: Paul Setinek; F. Paischer; Nils Thuerey; J. Brandstetter; Felix Koehler

page_placements.theme: Multi-fidelity simulation allocation depends on target and fidelity gap

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper draws on prior language-model scaling-law work and a Hoffmann et al. fitting approach to motivate and construct a calibration recipe. Its own results concern PDE-surrogate error and optimal simulation-fidelity mixtures, not the language-model scaling claims listed here.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results on PDE-surrogate error versus data-generation compute and on extrapolating optimal fidelity mixtures. These are related to, but do not measure, held-out language-model cross-entropy scaling, parameter/token allocation, or the other specified claim versions. Its references to language-model scaling laws are background and are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study trains PDE surrogates (FNO, U-Net, Transolver, AB-UPT) and measures relative L2 error against data-generation compute under different simulation-fidelity mixtures. It never fits or tests a power-law form for loss in parameters, tokens or training compute, for language models or for surrogates. It borrows Hoffmann et al.'s Approach 2 (Section K.1) only as a tool to fit its own log-linear Ansatz for the optimal mixture λ*, and reports that tool's regret. Its log-log scaling curves and the model-size ablation (Table 30) are not fitted to any power law, so they cannot bear on V5's 'same power-law form'. None of V1–V7 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that, at any finite data-generation budget, optimal fidelity mixtures outperform high-fidelity-only training, and that the two converge only at very large budgets. Savings average ~3.1× across 20 setups, up to 6.3×. They also find that the solver-error axis outperforms the discretization axis where resolution invariance is required, and recommend it to practitioners. Their λ* extrapolation recipe degrades on some discretization settings.
record.recipe_differences: The study adapts a scaling-law-inspired calibration idea to fit optimal simulation-fidelity mixture versus data-generation budget; it does not fit language-model loss power laws or allocate model parameters and tokens.
record.method_sensitivity: The optimal mixture and extrapolation quality vary with PDE, architecture, fidelity axis, and budget. The log-linear mixture Ansatz has large regret on some Poisson discretization transitions; solver-axis extrapolation is more reliable in the reported mesh experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Optimal multi-fidelity training cuts the data-generation budget needed at matched relative L2 error in all 20 setups: mean ~3.1×, up to 6.3×. The 95% bootstrap intervals all exclude 1×.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For PDE surrogates, mixing simulation fidelities reduces the data-generation compute needed at matched test error, compared with high-fidelity-only data.

fits_no_version.finding: A log-linear fit of λ* against log budget, using Hoffmann Approach 2, extrapolates with low regret on the solver axis (Table 27, ≤13.6%). It fails at abrupt transitions on Poisson discretization (Table 28: 70.3% and 99.2% for 2D U-Net).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimal fidelity mixtures extrapolate across budgets in a setup-dependent way and fail when the optimum jumps abruptly.

fits_no_version.finding: For the 2D Poisson U-Net (solver axis), the HF-only error floor falls monotonically from 4.0% to 1.4% as parameters grow from 0.69M to 43.65M (Table 30). Multi-fidelity savings stay at about 3×. No power law is fitted.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: PDE-surrogate error falls with model size, while multi-fidelity data savings stay roughly constant across model sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: At AB-UPT airfoil B̃≈200, multi-fidelity training lowers lift-coefficient error by 54.9% relative to HF-only training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-fidelity data gains carry over to derived engineering metrics.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 (40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)
record.problems: The paper studies PDE surrogates rather than language models and reports relative L2 or engineering-metric errors rather than held-out cross-entropy. The authors state that a full scaling-law analysis jointly varying model size, training compute, dataset-generation compute, and fidelity mixture is currently intractable. Their own extrapolation recipe degrades on some discretization-error settings, including abrupt Poisson transitions. The stated conclusions also assume data-generation cost dominates training cost and that models are large and trained long enough to absorb additional data.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Detailed per-budget and per-architecture tables are not exhaustively transcribed because they concern PDE-surrogate data-generation scaling rather than any named claim version; the selected rows capture the study's aggregate reported results and a stated downstream-metric result.

untested.parts: No language-model held-out loss. No power-law fit of loss in parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation of loss power laws. Only λ* is extrapolated, via a log-linear Ansatz.
No parameter/token allocation at a fixed training-compute budget. The allocation studied is across simulation fidelities under data-generation compute.
No comparison of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
PDE-surrogate error versus data budget and model size is reported, but no power-law form is fitted or tested.
No downstream-task predictability from scale or from pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits across setups or fitting methods.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Language-model scaling laws appear only as motivation and as a fitting tool (Hoffmann Approach 2). The authors explicitly decline a full scaling-law analysis as intractable. The training-duration ablation (L.5) hints that compute-optimal multi-fidelity models should be smaller and trained longer. This is speculation, not a test of V3.

versions.untested_parts: No language-model held-out pretraining loss or power-law dependence on parameters, tokens, or training compute is measured.
The paper extrapolates optimal fidelity mixtures, not small-run power-law fits predicting much larger language-model losses.
It studies allocation across simulation fidelities at a data-generation compute budget, not parameter and token counts at a language-model training compute budget.
No fixed-parameter language-model architecture comparison is reported.
Although PDE surrogates are a different application setting, the paper does not test whether the claimed language-model power-law form holds there.
It reports PDE-surrogate field and engineering-metric errors, not downstream language-model task performance or its predictability from pretraining loss or scale.
The paper studies setup-specific fidelity-mixture calibration, not dependence of language-model scaling exponents or parameter/token compute-optimal splits on fitting and training choices.
